what: HCA Healthcare runs hospitals. It operates about 190 hospitals and more than 120 surgery centres across 19 US states and England, treating patients and billing insurers, Medicare and Medicaid.
customers: Patients, but payment comes from commercial insurers, Medicare, Medicaid and self-paying patients.
money: inpatient admissions, emergency care and surgery
freestanding surgery and endoscopy centres and urgent care
moat: Dense hospital networks in fast-growing markets like Texas and Florida, which give it negotiating power with insurers in those regions.
risks: Debt of about $52 billion is high even for a hospital operator
Nursing and physician labour costs rise faster than reimbursement
Changes to Medicaid funding and state supplemental payments hit revenue directly
Uninsured patients produce bad debt that it cannot recover
opportunities: Population growth and ageing in its core states raise admission volumes
Shifting procedures to outpatient centres improves margins
It has used strong cash flow to buy back a very large share of its stock
watch: Same-facility admissions and revenue per admission, plus labour cost per patient day.
